text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Italian Prime Minister Prodi: Foreign aid cannot replace institutions.
--Prime Minister Hariri to Cairo to solve the "potatoes crisis". Egypt had protested against Lebanon's decision to ban the imports of Egyptian potatoes two weeks ago.
-Lebanese, Palestinian Moslem and leftist groups protested against the arrest of five Red Army guerrillas and urged the government to immediately release Kozo Okamoto.
Okamoto was involved in the May 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 24 people died and 100 were injured.
--The signing of a $500 million agreement related to financial aid and assistance between Lebanon and Italy was delayed.
--The ministry of interior began issuing new identification cards for the first time since the start of the 1975-90 civil war.
--A delegation of Italian businessmen visited the Beirut Chamber of Commerce, "Solidere" and the Council for Development and Reconstruction.
